q1: SELECT beer, MAX(price) - MIN(price) AS price_gap, AVG(price) AS avg_price FROM serves WHERE beer IN (SELECT s.beer FROM serves AS s, frequents AS f WHERE s.bar = f.bar AND f.drinker LIKE 'B%' GROUP BY s.beer HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT s.bar) >= 2) GROUP BY beer ORDER BY beer
q2: SELECT B.name AS beer, MIN(S.price) AS price, S.bar AS bar FROM Beer AS B LEFT JOIN Serves AS S ON B.name = S.beer GROUP BY B.name, S.bar

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 calculates the price gap and average price for beers that are served in at least two different bars and are frequently consumed by drinkers whose names start with 'B'. Q2, on the other hand, lists the name of each beer, the minimum price at which it is served, and the name of the bar where this minimum price is achieved.
